observations: Photo 0 shows a black UPS unit with 'BLUE GATE' embossed on the front panel. A blue vertical strip with a power button and three LED indicators is visible. The unit appears to be on a tiled floor.
Photo 1 shows the same unit from a side angle, with a black power cord plugged into a 3-pin plug on top. The unit is placed on a tiled floor. The side panel has ventilation slots.
The unit has a matte black finish with some minor scuffs and dust. The power button is round and centered on the blue strip. The LEDs are not illuminated in either photo.
No model number or serial number is visible in either photo.
The seller claims it is a UPS with a new battery and 8-hour charge time, and that it has never been repaired.

claims.evidence: The item is clearly a UPS unit as shown in both photos.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours. Never repaired.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The UPS may not be functional or may have a degraded battery or internal damage.
risks.proof: A video showing the UPS powering a device (e.g., a lamp or fan) while unplugged from the wall, and a photo of the battery indicator lights in operation.

risks.risk: The unit may be missing essential components (e.g., surge protection, AC adapter, or manual).
risks.proof: A photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the unit.

risks.risk: The unit may have internal damage or wear not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit being powered on and off, and a close-up of the internal components (if accessible).

proof_requests: Video of the UPS powering a device while unplugged from the wall.
Photo of the battery indicator lights in operation.
Photo of all included accessories (surge protector, AC adapter, manual, etc.).
Close-up of the model number or serial number if visible on the unit.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
